name: Marc-Andre Barriault
event: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott
summary: Quebec's 'PowerBar' (17-11, 1 NC; 6-10, 1 NC UFC), a 36-year-old pressure brawler who wins with volume, clinch work and toughness and has earned Fight of the Night in each of his last two fights while losing both. He is 1-5 in his last six and badly needs a win, likely to keep his roster spot.

how_they_fight.Striking: Relentless forward pressure and high volume (about 4.9 significant strikes a minute) with hooks, uppercuts and knees in the clinch. Per UFC.com, his strength is closing distance fast and creating chaotic exchanges. Also absorbs a lot (about 5.7 a minute). Hurt Michal Oleksiejczuk with clinch work in round two but lost 29-28 x3.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Rarely wrestles (about 0.6 takedowns per 15 minutes); his clinch is for striking. Has been taken down and submitted by a strong grappler (Anthony Hernandez, sub R3) and controlled by Sharabutdin Magomedov.
how_they_fight.Defense: Tough over three rounds but has been stopped early by power: Chidi Njokuani (R1, 0:16), Joe Pyfer (R1, 1:25), Dustin Stoltzfus (R1, 4:28). All three of his KO/TKO losses came in round one.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Gets better as the fight goes: his UFC stoppage wins came late in rounds (Abu Azaitar R3 at 4:56, Julian Marquez R2 at 4:12) or with an early blitz (Bruno Silva R1). Outworks people in round three. Danger zone is the first round, where all three of his KO losses happened.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Honest, all-action fighter with one gear; trades rather than manages. Prone to getting hit clean early while walking forward.

patterns: Pressure and volume; wins late rounds on output
Late-round stoppages: R3 (Azaitar) and R2 at 4:12 (Marquez); early blitz finish of Bruno Silva (R1)
All three KO/TKO losses came in round 1
Fight of the Night in each of his last two fights (both losses), per UFC.com
Seven of his 11 career losses are decisions
Knees in the clinch against a shooting opponent; survived the back and escaped to his feet
concerns: 1-5 in his last six fights; likely fighting for his job
Defensive leaks early against power punchers
Takedown and submission defense against a skilled grappler like Daukaus
Age (36) and accumulated damage from high-volume wars
keys_to_beat: Hurt him in round one before his pace builds
Take him down and work for submissions; he rarely threatens off his back
Avoid prolonged clinch exchanges against the fence

news.text: Booked against Kyle Daukaus at middleweight in Edmonton; Cageside notes he is 1-5 in his last six.
Lost a unanimous decision (29-28 x3) to Michal Oleksiejczuk at UFC Vegas 113 after a rough first round; Fight of the Night.
Media day: says he is in the last chapter of his career and wants 'good fights, good guys'; plans to 'bring the action' but be smart and 'lead the dance'.
Official weigh-in: 185 lb for the middleweight bout; no misses reported on the card.
Beat Kyle Daukaus by R1 TKO (knees and ground strikes) after escaping two minutes of back control.
